original_question: For Macdonald superpolynomials in superspace, does the automorphism rho_{q,t} satisfy the second duality relation rho_{q,t}(P_Lambda(q, t)) = t^{|Lambda'a|} Q_{Lambda'}(t, q) for every superpartition Lambda?
target_in_paper: The draft is not paper-faithful as written for arXiv:1903.07777. The nearest official formulation reviewed there is the established duality theorem for Macdonald polynomials in superspace: for every superpartition Λ, one has Ω_{q,t} P_Λ(q,t) = (q t^{-1})^{|Λ|} Q_{Λ'}(t^{-1}, q^{-1}). In the underlying source paper this is Section 5.3, Theorem 18.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the topic as Macdonald superpolynomials in superspace, asks for a duality statement indexed by the conjugate superpartition Λ', and uses the normalized Q-basis rather than only the P-basis. It also correctly quantifies over all superpartitions.
missing_details: The automorphism in the official statement is Ω_{q,t}, not ρ_{q,t}.

Ω_{q,t} must be defined explicitly on power sums by combining two homomorphisms: ω_{q,t}(p_r)=(-1)^{r-1}(1-q^r)/(1-t^r) p_r, ω_{q,t}(\tilde p_r)=(-1)^r \tilde p_r, \tilde\omega_q(p_r)=p_r, \tilde\omega_q(\tilde p_r)=q^r \tilde p_r, and Ω_{q,t}=\tilde\omega_q\circ\omega_{q,t}.

The ambient space is the ring R of symmetric functions in superspace over Q(q,t), with commuting variables x and anticommuting variables θ; the proof works componentwise in each finite-dimensional homogeneous piece R_{n,m}.
The normalization Q_Λ must be defined by Q_Λ=b_Λ(q,t) P_Λ(q,t), where b_Λ(q,t)=⟨⟨P_Λ(q,t),P_Λ(q,t)⟩⟩_{q,t}^{-1}.
The parameters on the right-hand side are inverted: the official theorem has Q_{Λ'}(t^{-1},q^{-1}), not Q_{Λ'}(t,q).
The prefactor is (q t^{-1})^{|Λ|}, not t^{|Λ'^a|}.
The statement is presented in the paper as a proved duality theorem, not as a conjectural 'second duality relation'.
The notation Λ' means the conjugate superpartition; this should be stated explicitly.

Because conventions vary across later summaries, one should not insert extra signs or altered prefactors unless one also changes the scalar product convention; the original theorem has exactly the factor shown above.
refined_question: Let R be the ring of symmetric functions in superspace over Q(q,t), with commuting variables x, anticommuting variables θ, power sums p_r and \tilde p_r, and let Ω_{q,t}=\tilde\omega_q\circ\omega_{q,t} be the automorphism defined by ω_{q,t}(p_r)=(-1)^{r-1}(1-q^r)/(1-t^r)\,p_r, ω_{q,t}(\tilde p_r)=(-1)^r\,\tilde p_r, \tilde\omega_q(p_r)=p_r, and \tilde\omega_q(\tilde p_r)=q^r\,\tilde p_r. If Q_Λ=b_Λ(q,t)P_Λ(q,t), with b_Λ(q,t)=⟨⟨P_Λ(q,t),P_Λ(q,t)⟩⟩_{q,t}^{-1}, is it true that for every superpartition Λ one has the duality formula Ω_{q,t}P_Λ(q,t)=(q t^{-1})^{|Λ|}Q_{Λ'}(t^{-1},q^{-1})?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, as stated in the proof of Theorem 18, does one have ⟨⟨Ω_{q,t}^{-1}P_{Λ'}(t^{-1},q^{-1}) \mid P_Ω(q,t)⟩⟩_{q,t}=\delta_{Λ,Ω} for all superpartitions Λ,Ω?
justification: The draft is aiming at the superspace analog of Macdonald duality, but it conflates that theorem with a different notation/convention. In the precise source statement, the operator is Ω_{q,t}, not ρ_{q,t}; the right-hand side involves parameter inversion (t^{-1},q^{-1}); and the scalar factor is (q t^{-1})^{|Λ|}. The paper treats this as a theorem, proved in the duality subsection, not as an open conjecture. The proof also makes clear an equivalent inner-product formulation, so that is the only alternate formulation worth keeping.
